name: The Clockwork Arena
concept_focus: A full game engine, then agents that play it: search, evaluation and tournaments

story.title: The Clockwork Arena
story.client: Old Tobin, keeper of the Clockwork Arena
story.hook: Tobin's arena pits clockwork engines against each other at Connect Four. One engine, the Grandmaster, has never lost, and it has started playing the hunters too. Build the game from nothing, then build engines of your own, smarter each act, until one of them can sit across from the Grandmaster.

acts.title: Act I: The Board
acts.goal: Build Connect Four itself: the grid, dropping pieces, finding a winner, two players taking turns.

acts.title: Act II: First Engines
acts.goal: Give every player one interface, then build a random engine, a rule-following engine and a way to record games.

acts.title: Act III: Thinking Ahead
acts.goal: Teach an engine to search: minimax, an evaluation function, alpha-beta pruning and a time budget.

acts.title: Act IV: The Tournament
acts.goal: Run tournaments, rate every engine, tune your best one against itself, and open the arena to spectators.

boss_lore: The Grandmaster does not think faster than you. It simply never forgets to look one move further.
boss_brief: Bring a finished connect_four.py: full rules, human, random, greedy and minimax-with-alpha-beta engines behind one interface, a time budget, a round-robin tournament with Elo ratings, and an engine that beats your greedy one almost every game.

mobs.name: The Empty Grid
mobs.concept: Nested lists as a game board
mobs.encounter: Build a 6 by 7 board and draw it in the terminal.
mobs.contract: The arena floor is bare: six rows, seven columns, nothing in them. Lay out the grid and make it visible.

objectives.label: Build the board
objectives.brief: Write a function in connect_four.py that returns a new 6 by 7 board as a list of lists, every cell empty.

objectives.label: Draw the board
objectives.brief: Print the board with clear symbols for empty cells and both players, and the column numbers underneath.

objectives.label: Catch the shared-row trap
objectives.brief: Explain why building the board with [[' '] * 7] * 6 makes every row change together, and show your board does not.

mobs.name: The Falling Stone
mobs.concept: Searching a column from the bottom up
mobs.encounter: Drop a piece into a column so it lands on the lowest empty cell.
mobs.contract: Stones fall, they do not float. Make every piece land where gravity puts it, and refuse a column that is already full.

objectives.label: Drop a piece
objectives.brief: Write drop_piece(board, column, piece) that places the piece in the lowest empty cell of that column.

objectives.label: Refuse a full column
objectives.brief: Make dropping into a full or out-of-range column fail clearly instead of crashing or overwriting a piece, and explain how you detect it.

objectives.label: List legal moves
objectives.brief: Write legal_moves(board) that returns the columns a piece can still be dropped into.

mobs.name: The Four Seers
mobs.concept: Scanning a grid in four directions
mobs.encounter: Find four in a row across, down and on both diagonals.
mobs.contract: Four seers watch the board, one for each direction a line can run. Until all four are watching, a winner can walk away unnoticed.

objectives.label: Check across and down
objectives.brief: Write a winner check that finds four of the same piece in a row horizontally and vertically.

objectives.label: Check both diagonals
objectives.brief: Extend it to both diagonal directions, rising and falling.

objectives.label: Guard the edges
objectives.brief: Explain why a negative index such as board[row][-1] can make your check see a line that wraps around the grid, and show how your loops stay inside the board.

mobs.name: The Two-Player Table
mobs.concept: A turn loop with validation and an end
mobs.encounter: Let two people play a full game in the terminal.
mobs.contract: Two hunters, one board. Make them take turns honestly, stop at four in a row or a full grid, and survive whatever they type.

objectives.label: Alternate the turns
objectives.brief: Run a full game where two players alternate, the board is shown each turn, and the game stops when someone wins.

objectives.label: Declare a draw
objectives.brief: End the game as a draw when the board fills with no winner.

objectives.label: Survive bad input
objectives.brief: Ask again on text, out-of-range numbers or a full column, without losing the player's turn or crashing.

mobs.name: The Mask Maker
mobs.concept: One interface for every kind of player
mobs.encounter: Make every player a function that is given the board and returns a column.
mobs.contract: Behind every mask in the arena is the same face: a function that sees the board and names a column. Carve the mask, and humans and engines can take the same seat.

objectives.label: Define the agent shape
objectives.brief: Turn players into agents: functions agent(board, piece) that return a column. Wrap the human's input() in one.

objectives.label: Play agent against agent
objectives.brief: Write play_game(agent_a, agent_b) that runs a game between any two agents and returns the winner or a draw.

objectives.label: Explain the mask
objectives.brief: Explain why giving every player the same function shape lets you swap humans and engines without touching the game loop.

mobs.name: The Drunken Automaton
mobs.encounter: Build a random engine and play a thousand games.
mobs.contract: The oldest engine in the arena staggers between columns at random. It is useless as a player and priceless as a baseline.

objectives.label: Build the random engine
objectives.brief: Write random_agent, which picks one of the legal moves at random.

objectives.label: Play a thousand games
objectives.brief: Play 1,000 random-against-random games without printing the boards and count wins for each side and draws.

objectives.label: Read the first-move edge
objectives.brief: Explain from your counts whether moving first is an advantage, and why random play still shows it.

mobs.name: The Watchful Guard
mobs.concept: Looking one move ahead on a copy
mobs.encounter: Build an engine that wins when it can and blocks when it must.
mobs.contract: The Guard is no genius. It just never misses a win in one and never lets you have one. Most players lose to that alone.

objectives.label: Test moves on a copy
objectives.brief: Write a helper that tries a move on a copy of the board and reports whether it wins, leaving the real board untouched.

objectives.label: Win, block, else centre
objectives.brief: Write greedy_agent: take a winning move if there is one, otherwise block the opponent's winning move, otherwise prefer the centre column.

objectives.label: Find the leaking test
objectives.brief: Explain what goes wrong if the engine tries moves on the real board (or a shallow copy of it), and how your copy avoids it.

objectives.label: Prove it beats random
objectives.brief: Play 200 games of greedy_agent against random_agent, swapping who goes first, and report its win rate.

mobs.name: The Replay Scribe
mobs.encounter: Save every game as a list of moves and replay it later.
mobs.contract: Tobin keeps a scribe who writes down every move ever played in the arena. Lose a game and the scribe can show you exactly where.

objectives.label: Record the moves
objectives.brief: Make play_game also return the list of columns played, in order, with which agents played.

objectives.label: Save games to JSON
objectives.brief: Save finished games to a JSON file as dictionaries with the players, the moves and the result.

objectives.label: Replay a game
objectives.brief: Load a saved game and replay it move by move on a fresh board, showing the board after each move.

mobs.name: The Branching Oracle
mobs.encounter: Search the game tree a few moves deep and pick the best move.
mobs.contract: The Oracle sees every future branch a few moves deep: every move you could make, every reply. It picks the branch where its worst case is best.

objectives.label: Write minimax
objectives.brief: Write a recursive minimax(board, depth, maximizing) that returns a score, with wins, losses and draws as terminal scores.

objectives.label: Turn it into an engine
objectives.brief: Write minimax_agent, which scores every legal move with minimax and plays the best one.

objectives.label: Count the branches
objectives.brief: Predict how many positions a depth-2 search visits from an empty board, then count it in your code.

mobs.name: The Weigher of Windows
mobs.concept: An evaluation function from many small windows
mobs.encounter: Score positions that are not finished yet.
mobs.contract: Search runs out of depth long before the game ends. The Weigher judges an unfinished board by looking through every window of four cells.

objectives.label: Collect every window
objectives.brief: Collect every line of four cells on the board, in all four directions.

objectives.label: Weigh the windows
objectives.brief: Score each window from a dictionary of weights (three of yours and an empty, two and two empties, the opponent's threats) plus a centre-column bonus, and use it when the search stops early.

objectives.label: Defend your weights
objectives.brief: Explain why an opponent's three-in-a-window should count against you more than your own two counts for you.

mobs.name: The Pruner
mobs.encounter: Make the search skip branches that cannot matter.
mobs.contract: Half the Oracle's visions are branches no sane player would take. The Pruner cuts them off before they are explored.

objectives.label: Add alpha-beta
objectives.brief: Add alpha and beta bounds to your search and stop exploring a branch as soon as it cannot change the result.

objectives.label: Count what was saved
objectives.brief: Count the positions visited with and without pruning at the same depth and report both.

objectives.label: Prove nothing changed
objectives.brief: Check that the pruned search picks a move with the same score as plain minimax on several boards, and explain what a mismatch would mean.

mobs.name: The Hourglass
mobs.concept: Iterative deepening and a time budget
mobs.encounter: Search as deep as time allows, then move.
mobs.contract: In the arena every engine gets one turn of the hourglass. Think too long and you forfeit. Think in rings, deeper each time, and keep your best answer ready.

objectives.label: Order the moves
objectives.brief: Search centre columns first and show it lets pruning cut more branches.

objectives.label: Deepen step by step
objectives.brief: Search depth 1, then 2, then 3 and so on, keeping the best move from the last finished depth.

objectives.label: Stop when time runs out
objectives.brief: Stop searching when a time limit passes and still return a legal move, and explain what happens if the limit hits in the middle of a depth.

mobs.name: The Arena Clerk
mobs.encounter: Make every engine play every other, both colours.
mobs.contract: The Clerk books every match: each engine against each other, white and black, many times over. No engine ducks a rival.

objectives.label: Book every match
objectives.brief: Run a round-robin where every engine plays every other engine several times as each colour.

objectives.label: Print the table
objectives.brief: Print a results table of wins, losses and draws per engine, sorted best first.

objectives.label: Explain the colours
objectives.brief: Explain why every pairing must play both colours for the table to be fair.

mobs.name: The Ratings Keeper
mobs.encounter: Give every engine an Elo rating.
mobs.contract: Wins against weaklings prove little. The Keeper's ratings rise most when you beat someone who should have beaten you.

objectives.label: Update Elo
objectives.brief: After each tournament game, update both engines' Elo ratings from the expected and actual result.

objectives.label: Show the ratings
objectives.brief: Show every engine's rating after the tournament, and save it so the next tournament starts from there.

objectives.label: Trace one update
objectives.brief: Predict whether a 1500 engine gains more points for beating a 1700 engine or a 1300 one, then check your function.

mobs.name: The Mirror Match
mobs.encounter: Improve your evaluation weights by playing your engine against itself.
mobs.contract: The only opponent who knows your engine's flaws is your engine. Set it against slightly changed copies of itself and keep whichever wins.

objectives.label: Make variants
objectives.brief: Make engines that share your search but use slightly changed evaluation weights.

objectives.label: Keep the winner
objectives.brief: Play each variant against the current best over many games and keep whichever wins clearly, for several rounds.

objectives.label: Spot the trap
objectives.brief: Explain how an engine tuned only against itself could still lose to a different style of player.

mobs.name: The Spectator's Box
mobs.encounter: Open the arena: a menu to play, watch and run tournaments.
mobs.contract: Tobin wants the stands full. Let people play your engines at the difficulty they choose, watch engines duel move by move, and run the tournament themselves.

objectives.label: Let people watch
objectives.brief: Add a watch mode where two engines play with the board shown after every move and a short pause between moves.

objectives.label: Choose a difficulty
objectives.brief: Let a human pick easy, medium or hard, which sets the engine and its search depth or time budget.

objectives.label: Open the menu
objectives.brief: Add a start menu: play an engine, watch a duel, run a tournament, replay a saved game, or quit.
